page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 12 dedicated vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. It includes 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the Geekbench multi-core score of 4589.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 10042.2. Memory bandwidth remains moderate, with uncached large-block read speeds at 56.47 GB/sec and write speeds at 44.31 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector operations benefit from hardware-level support for AES, AVX, and AVX512F instructions.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads that do not demand high single-thread performance. Suitable applications include multi-threaded compilation, Redis caching layers, and moderate database operations. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which aligns with its 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio provide predictable compute resources for legacy enterprise applications, though modern workloads requiring high-throughput single-core execution or local NVMe storage may find better resource density elsewhere.
